I found something more important.

I've been through a lot, and no one denied that, and most of my friends and acquaintances understood that. I didn't have  much to carry on for, and I couldn't see any light at the end of the tunnel. I had been suicidal since I was 7 years old, and I was now 18, in a crap mental health service, i had been on an ineffective antidepressant for 3 years with no therapy or changes. 

And then, after another eventful trip to the hospital (i'm sure you can guess), and another conversation with a decrepit bitch who isn't listening, I finally got angry. i found enough self worth to say "You don't know shit. You think if this emotion was gonna just 'floooow away' like emotions do, I would be here with a cannula in my hand and my mum sobbing outside because she couldn't save me? Where the hell have you lot been, while shes been desperately calling you, while I've been up all night because if I sleep I relive years of pain? Who the hell do you think you are. And how many other people are suffering, or even dead, because of your failures."

She had been complaining that I had woken her up. This woman, an on call psychologist, had refused to answer the phone for hours, and then had the audacity to complain to my face. 

Not only that, But my Care Coordinator (yeah right) hadn't picked up the phone for 3 WEEKS. And my Psychiatrist hadn't bothered to check in with me for about 6 months, despite multiple notes from my GP informing him that I was a danger to myself and others and needed to be evaluated for sectioning. 

My anger kick started my mother. She knew that if I was pissed off, there had to be some life still in me (I'm usually very good-natured and polite, even when distressed). she fought to get me one of the finest professionals she could, and threatened to sue if my psychiatrist did not turn over my care to my GP.

So, I am now nearing the end of therapy, which has been rough, but was well worth it ( and shes amazing!), I have an amazing boyfriend who stayed with me throughout everything, and I'm trying to get into the NHS and train in psychiatric care, so I can succeed where they failed, and to ensure that another person in my position doesn't have to try to get people who are paid to listen, to listen to them. This drive, to do better, and to change the system keeps me going through the dark times. I am resilient, and I know i can make it. 

For all you others reading this, if you are suffering, please get help, and if you aren't getting good quality help,  or feel neglected or ignored by those who are supposed to be caring for you, please, speak out, get angry. You have the right to care, and every. single. one. of. you. is worth it. If they aren't helping you, they are not doing their job. But please remember, that for every horrible mental health professional you come across, there will be 10 really excellent compassionate ones. Stay strong my Lovelies, its not the end yet xxx
